messages:
Maria: Quick note from today's oncall: a customer hit a silent corruption after a partial push of safetensors shards. We should probably standardize a lightweight per-shard checksum + signed manifest scheme. Thoughts?
Devin: Agreed. Right now we only verify top-level manifest checksum. Per-shard would let loaders fail fast instead of producing NaNs later.
Sparrow: We need to be careful about perf: adding a large CRC per shard is fine but verifying at read time for every read could blow IO. Maybe store a small 64-bit siphash and do verification only on first read/hotstart.
Chao: Also consider streaming reads: if we sign a manifest that includes per-shard checksums, but the shards are streamed (range requests), the client has to be able to verify partial ranges. We can do chunk-level checksums (e.g., 4MB chunk hashes) and a Merkle root in the shard header.
Nora: Chunk-level + Merkle sounds robust but increases metadata. Maybe make it optional: manifest declares checksum_scheme: none|crc32|chunked-merkle and loader picks based on policy. Backcompat: default none.
Maria: I like optional scheme. For Hosted we can require chunked-merkle for high integrity; for Dedicated we can default to crc32 for smaller overhead.
Devin: Implementation note: for safetensors files we can add a small trailing sidecar (.safetensors.meta) or embed a compact header in the shard preface with a magic and version. Sidecar easier for backwards compatibility.
Sparrow: Sidecar helps rollouts, yes. But when streaming through CDN, sidecars must be colocated. If sidecar missing, loader should fallback to manifest checksum or fetch entire shard and verify.
Chao: Security: signing. Use a manifest JWT signed by the publishing key. Loader verifies manifest signature before trusting checksums. That prevents a MITM swapping shard data + checksum. We should include manifest_pubkey_id in the manifest for key lookup.
Nora: Key rotation: include a key history array in the control plane and a short-lived signing policy. Loaders should cache verified keys and refetch on signature failures. Ops-bot can we make a ticket for key rotation docs?
ops-bot: INF-3077 created: "Manifest signing and key rotation playbook". Will track docs + key service changes.
Devin: Performance: Merkle verification on first read is O(n) CPU. Need a fast path: if the inode already has a verified xattr (from earlier ingest) skip verify. For streaming reads from remote, verify progressively as chunks arrive and fail early on mismatch.
Sparrow: UX: manifest should include checksum_scheme and a per-shard field checksum_meta_uri (or inline small JSON). Example manifest snippet:
```json
{"shards":[{"path":"m.safetensors.000","checksum_scheme":"chunked-merkle","checksum_meta_uri":"/meta/m.000.meta"}]}
```
Chao: Testing: simulate corrupted middle-chunk both for local NVMe and CDN streaming. Ensure loaders abort with clear error and metrics: shard.verify.fail_reason.
Maria: Action items: Devin draft manifest fields + signing proposal; Sparrow add loader verification fast-paths & progressive chunk verify; Chao build corruption sim; Nora coordinate key rotation docs; ops-bot will track INF-3077.
Devin: I'll open the draft tonight.
Sparrow: I'll add a small benchmark to check first-read CPU cost for merkle vs crc32.
Maria: Nice work. Let's keep chunked-merkle opt-in for now until perf numbers look good. :thumbsup:
